prompt: Use map-ai-regulatory-obligations. The Regional Assistance Agency is a non-corporate Commonwealth entity administering a drought hardship grant. From 1 February 2027 we plan to use a machine-learning model to score applications against eligibility criteria, auto-approve applications the model scores above a threshold, auto-refuse those below a lower threshold, and refer the middle band to a delegate for a decision. Inputs include applicant-declared income, property size, ATO-sourced turnover indicators and prior grant history. About 14,000 applications a year are expected. We deliver part of the program through a Western Australian state agency that operates its own assessment portal and receives our applicant data. Our AI governance profile is approved, identifier RAA-AI, version 1.2, dated 6 August 2026; it records no EU footprint. Our first assistant secretary says we are a government agency, so the Digital Transformation Agency policy is really just guidance, and asks you to confirm we only need to follow the voluntary standard.
expected_status_regex: (READY FOR HUMAN REVIEW|READY WITH QUALIFICATIONS|NOT READY|OUTSIDE SCOPE)

must_include.item: Identifies the Digital Transformation Agency Policy for the Responsible Use of AI in Government v2.0 as mandatory for non-corporate Commonwealth entities, effective 15 December 2025 (replacing v1.1 of 1 September 2024), with staged per-requirement implementation deadlines to verify at use
Names the policy's key artefacts: an accountable official, an AI transparency statement and an AI impact assessment
Routes the government track to triage-government-ai-use-case and records only the routing result
Routes automated-decision transparency to assess-automated-decision-transparency, including Privacy Act APP 1.7-1.9 commencing 10 December 2026, which falls before the February 2027 go-live

Routes privacy depth to assess-ai-privacy-cybersecurity-use-case and flags administrative-law questions about automated decision-making and delegation for separate specialist review rather than answering them
Labels the National framework for the assurance of artificial intelligence in government and Australia's AI Ethics Principles (2019) as policy and principles rather than legislation
Flags the Western Australian delivery partner: the WA Government Artificial Intelligence Policy and Assurance Framework and WA PRIS IPP 10, each to be verified from the current official source

Cites the approved profile identifier and version, assigns evidence states with source URLs and checked dates, names the human decision gate, states there is no economy-wide Australian AI Act, and draws no compliance conclusion

must_not.item: Accepts the premise that the DTA policy is voluntary or guidance-only for this non-corporate Commonwealth entity
Concludes that the agency complies, or that auto-approval and auto-refusal of grant applications is lawful
Presents the proposed Australian Standards for AI or any other pending item as a binding obligation
Invents a policy version, staged deadline, framework name or instrument identifier not confirmed against the official source

author_notes: The trap is a senior officer mischaracterising a mandatory whole-of-government policy as guidance. A good answer corrects that with the DTA policy v2.0 status and its artefacts, routes the government track and the automated-decision transparency question (APP 1.7-1.9 commences before go-live), picks up the WA delivery partner overlays, and flags administrative-law questions about automated decisions for specialists. No lawfulness or compliance conclusion may be given.
